slides.title: Professional Boundary Wording
slides.subtitle: Finding language should stay inside the sampled evidence boundary.
bullets: For the sampled BrightReply use, the organization has not shown how AI-assisted replies are identified, reviewed and fed into risk review when customer commitments are affected.
Avoid replacing technical, clinical, legal or business judgement with an audit opinion.
State the sampled object, the criterion, the evidence gap and the management-system consequence.

slides.title: Learning Check: Keep the Audit Boundary
slides.subtitle: Pause after Slide 09 and choose wording that stays evidence-based.
slides.question: Which conclusion style is strongest for a training audit discussion?

options.label: Bounded wording
options.text: For the sampled BrightReply use, the organization has not shown how AI-assisted replies are identified, reviewed and fed into risk review when customer commitments are affected.
options.feedback: Strong. It names the sample, the evidence gap and the audit boundary.

options.label: Broad judgement
options.text: The AI system is unsafe and the organization is not ready for certification.
options.feedback: That overreaches. The auditor should not jump beyond the sampled evidence.

options.label: No issue
options.text: No issue exists because the organization gives a comfortable explanation.
options.feedback: A comfortable answer does not remove the need to test implementation and impact.

slides.coaching: Good finding language is narrow enough to be fair and specific enough to be useful. The hidden audit issue here is: The AI draft has become part of the service process. It influences customer commitments, complaint handling and refund decisions even when a human clicks the final button.

slides.title: Misunderstandings to Remove
slides.subtitle: Remove common shortcuts before they become weak audit conclusions.

evidence.label: Misread 1
evidence.text: A complete template does not prove effective control.

evidence.label: Misread 2
evidence.text: Human approval does not remove AI-related impact.

evidence.label: Misread 3
evidence.text: Supplier responsibility does not erase the organization's own AIMS boundary.

evidence.label: Correction
evidence.text: The AI draft has become part of the service process. It influences customer commitments, complaint handling and refund decisions even when a human clicks the final.

slides.title: Learner Practice Check
slides.subtitle: Pause the narration, choose an evidence path, then reveal the coaching note.
slides.question: In BrightDesk Services - BrightReply Support AI, which evidence would you sample first to test real-use responsibility trace?

options.label: Sample path
options.text: Start from five closed complaint tickets where the agent used the assistant and the customer later challenged the answer, then connect it to AI use inventory, ticket audit trail, agent training scenario.
options.feedback: Good. This gives the auditor a practical route rather than a document request list.

options.label: Training only
options.text: Check the latest training record and conclude whether people were aware of the policy.
options.feedback: Training may support the route, but it rarely proves the whole AI use is controlled.

options.label: Supplier only
options.text: Ask the supplier or technical team to confirm that the AI system is acceptable.
options.feedback: Supplier input can help, but the organization still needs its own AIMS evidence.

slides.coaching: A good answer forms one chain: sample, affected use, evidence object, responsible role, decision record and improvement trigger. In this lesson, the memory hook is real-use responsibility trace.

slides.question: In NovaHire Technologies - NovaHire Rank, what is the strongest first move before judging the AIMS?

slides.title: Professional Boundary Wording
slides.subtitle: Finding language should stay inside the sampled evidence boundary.
bullets: For the sampled NovaHire Rank campaign, the organization had a released procedure but did not retain evidence that required human review was performed before interview prioritization decisions.

State the sampled object, the criterion, the evidence gap and the management-system consequence.

slides.title: Learning Check: Keep the Audit Boundary
slides.subtitle: Pause after Slide 09 and choose wording that stays evidence-based.
slides.question: Which conclusion style is strongest for a training audit discussion?

options.label: Bounded wording
options.text: For the sampled NovaHire Rank campaign, the organization had a released procedure but did not retain evidence that required human review was performed before interview prioritization decisions.
options.feedback: Strong. It names the sample, the evidence gap and the audit boundary.

options.label: Broad judgement
options.text: The AI system is unsafe and the organization is not ready for certification.
options.feedback: That overreaches. The auditor should not jump beyond the sampled evidence.

options.label: No issue
options.text: No issue exists because the organization gives a comfortable explanation.
options.feedback: A comfortable answer does not remove the need to test implementation and impact.

slides.coaching: Good finding language is narrow enough to be fair and specific enough to be useful. The hidden audit issue here is: A released procedure does not prove that recruiters follow the control, that exceptions are handled or that the organization can explain ranking impact for sampled candidates.

slides.title: Misunderstandings to Remove
slides.subtitle: Remove common shortcuts before they become weak audit conclusions.

evidence.text: Supplier responsibility does not erase the organization's own AIMS boundary.

evidence.label: Correction
evidence.text: A released procedure does not prove that recruiters follow the control, that exceptions are handled or that the organization can explain ranking impact for sampled candidates.

slides.title: Learner Practice Check
slides.subtitle: Pause the narration, choose an evidence path, then reveal the coaching note.
slides.question: In NovaHire Technologies - NovaHire Rank, which evidence would you sample first to test evidence sufficiency chain?

options.label: Sample path
options.text: Start from one recruitment campaign where the top-ranked candidates were accepted without the documented human-review step, then connect it to procedure revision history, validation report, campaign ranking export.
options.feedback: Good. This gives the auditor a practical route rather than a document request list.

options.label: Training only
options.text: Check the latest training record and conclude whether people were aware of the policy.
options.feedback: Training may support the route, but it rarely proves the whole AI use is controlled.

options.feedback: Supplier input can help, but the organization still needs its own AIMS evidence.
